spec.title: A Gradle build reads offline a library the resolver fetched, through the readiness view's file repository
spec.description: Delayed setup for an ordinary Gradle build, on a real one. S48's gate passed with a replay that brings its own file mirror; an ordinary Gradle build has none, reads a remote repository's modules offline only from Gradle's own cache, and the resolver lays what it fetches in Maven's layout. Every readiness view now carries an init script (jobs/readiness.py, GRADLE_INIT) that gives the build a file repository over the modules a resolution fetched, laid apart in Maven's layout. gate.py shows it on Spring Boot's core module at S48's parent pin (example 635): the S cache is laid without org.jspecify:jspecify in Gradle's file store, in Gradle's descriptors and in Maven's local repository, a consumer job needs the operation in readiness-operation.json and waits while an unrelated job finishes, one resolution job, admitted by a commit, runs ':core:spring-boot:compileJava' offline until Gradle names the library, fetches its POM, its Gradle module metadata and its JAR from Maven Central (each by the repository's SHA-1), proves the compile offline in a network namespace with loopback alone and publishes the bundle, and the consumer then compiles the module itself with no network. Its compiled.json (the pin, the number of classes, the digest of one class) must be byte for byte what the resolution's own offline run wrote, and compile.sh fails if either Gradle cache holds the library after the build, so the file repository is the only place it can have been read from. One first-format job, because the default checkout's runner is the pipeline of before this line; the scheduler under test runs inside it, in a throwaway repository, without isolation of its own. It fetches three small files from Maven Central once. This is the gate's second run. In the first (20261128-011602) the file repository was over the view's whole Maven-layout folder, which holds the base's Maven local repository: Gradle read the fetched library from it, then took the POM of plexus-utils from it too, found no JAR beside it and looked nowhere else, though its own cache had the module whole. The repository is now over the fetched modules alone.
spec.expected: exit 0: every check of the gate passed (readiness-gate.json lists each with what was seen): one request, the consumer alone waiting, one resolution job, the library fetched with its Gradle module metadata, and the consumer's compile equal to the resolution's
